Subject: Inference enclosure — topology + SIG asks

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough. Our security team wants a concise package showing how Redwood isolates inference workloads for Private and Dedicated customers — specifically: the lattice (tenant-plane) model, the airlock/egress controls, and a SIG-friendly mapping of controls to our key risks.

Could you send:
- a single-page topology PNG (showing control plane vs data plane, interconnect, and egress gateways)
- a short segregation matrix (who can talk to what) in XLSX
- a one-page narrative we can drop into our SIG (CAIQ) question set

Target for our audit intake: 2028-03-20. Do you foresee any blockers?

Appreciate it — Tara
Security Architect
Orion HealthTech

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Inference enclosure — topology + SIG asks

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver that package; attaching the first pass of the topology and a segregation matrix draft. High-level notes below to accompany the attachments.

Attachment stubs: lattice-airlock-v1.png (PNG, 1.4MB) — single-sheet topology showing:
  * Control plane (Redwood-managed) separated from customer data plane (private VPC or dedicated pool)
  * Lattice overlay: per-tenant routing + enforcement layer; tenants are isolated via namespace + crypto-bound tokens (KMS-per-tenant where customer opts in)
  * Airlock egress gateway: outbound only, policy-enforced, TLS-inspecting (optional) with allowlist and S3/Blob storage targets; NATed egress sits in customer-dedicated subnet for Private deployments

segregation-matrix-v2.xlsx (XLSX) — rows: component, column: who/what can access, control owner, evidence pointer

One-page narrative (pasted below) — use as SIG answer:

--- Narrative (SIG-friendly) ---
Redwood infers models in a dual-plane architecture. The Control Plane (Redwood-managed) handles orchestration, model catalog, telemetry, and billing; it does not process unencrypted customer inference payloads. The Data Plane (customer workloads) is instantiated in Private deployments (customer VPCs or on-prem) or in Dedicated pools logically pinned to a customer. We enforce isolation using a three-layer approach:
1) Lattice enforcement: per-tenant logical slices implemented through namespace routing, mTLS identities, and network ACLs. For Dedicated pools the runtime uses per-tenant process sandboxes and hardware binding to limit cross-tenant access to model weights and KV caches.
2) Airlock egress: all outbound traffic from Data Plane flows through verifiable airlock gateways controlled by customer policy. Egress is explicit (deny-by-default), logged to immutable storage, and tied to retention controls for forensics.
3) Crypto & key separation: customer-managed KMS integration is supported; when enabled, model encryption keys and token signing keys are segregated per customer.

Controls are mapped to SIG/CAIQ evidence by artifact (config snapshots, network diagrams, firewall ACL exports, egress logs). We will produce an evidence index linking each claim to artifacts and screenshots.

Deliverables ETA: initial package by 2028-03-14 EOD, final by 2028-03-19 after your review comments.

Let us know if Helio (audit team) needs a runbook or live session to walkthrough.

— Mateo
Senior Infrastructure Architect
Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational clarifications before we finalize:

1) For Private VPCs we will include a sample VPC peering policy and a text snippet showing VPC route tables that implement the airlock (egress subnet + NAT gateway).
2) For Dedicated pools, note that the KV cache never crosses tenant boundaries; we will attach a runtime log extract demonstrating eviction and KV-access controls.
3) SIG mapping: I've attached a compact spreadsheet (segregation-matrix-v2.xlsx) with suggested CAIQ questions, our short answers, and pointer IDs to the evidence bundle (we'll export as sig-answer-summary-ORION.pdf).
